column1: Knowledge

The demo as-of date is 2026-10-15. The latest reported quarter is Q2 2026 which ends 2026-06-30; private-capital figures arrive 45 to 90 days after quarter end so Q3 2026 is not published yet. Questions about the latest quarter or current performance refer to the 2026-06-30 rows.

Harborline Private Capital is a fictional producer of private-markets benchmarks and indices (the Harborline Private Capital Index family or HPCI). It collects fund cash flows and NAVs contributed by LPs and GPs and extracts figures from GP quarterly reports. It does not manage money.

The universe holds 377 funds from 116 managers across six strategies (Buyout Growth Venture Private Credit Real Estate Infrastructure) and four regions (North America Europe Asia-Pacific Global) with vintages 2012 to 2024. Quarterly rows run from each fund's first capital call to 2026-06-30 (58 quarter ends in total).

Vintage year is the year of the fund's first capital call (Harborline convention) not the year of first close. Fund size equals total LP commitments in USD millions. All amounts are USD millions converted at the reporting date.
Size buckets by fund size: SMALL under 1 billion USD; MID_MARKET 1 to 5 billion; MEGA over 5 billion. Users say mid-market or middle market for MID_MARKET and mega or large for MEGA.

A custom index is any pooled cohort of funds selected by strategy region vintage range and size bucket. V_COHORT_INDEX_QUARTERLY pre-computes every cohort by strategy region vintage year size bucket and quarter; to combine cohorts sum TOTAL_NAV TOTAL_CALLED and TOTAL_DISTRIBUTED and recompute the ratios. The headline comparison statistic is the median fund IRR; the published Harborline indices use capital-weighted (pooled) IRR.

The broad PE benchmark is HPCI-BROAD-PE the Harborline Broad Private Equity Index: every buyout growth and venture fund in all regions and vintages. HPCI-ALL-PC the Harborline Private Capital Composite adds private credit real estate and infrastructure. Each fund also has a matching strategy-and-region index in FUNDS.BENCHMARK_ID (for example HPCI-BUYOUT-NA).

Index rows exist per vintage cohort (VINTAGE_YEAR) and for all vintages pooled (VINTAGE_YEAR NULL shown as VINTAGE_COHORT = All vintages). Comparing a fund or an allocator sleeve to its benchmark means the matching index at the same vintage year and quarter end.

The North American buyout custom index of vintages 2015 to 2020 holds 49 funds. At 2026-06-30 its median IRR is 15.9 percent against 13.3 percent for the Harborline Broad Private Equity Index (all vintages pooled) and its pooled TVPI is 1.58. Mid-market funds in that cohort have a median IRR of 16.3 percent versus 13.1 percent for mega funds.

A subscription credit line (subscription line or capital call facility or line of credit) is borrowing secured on undrawn LP commitments that a GP uses to bridge capital calls. FUNDS.USES_SUBSCRIPTION_LINE flags the funds that have one SUBSCRIPTION_LINE_LIMIT_USD_M is the facility size and FUND_QUARTERLY_NAV.CREDIT_LINE_BALANCE_USD_M is the drawn balance at each quarter end. 156 of 377 funds use a line and 89 funds had a balance drawn at 2026-06-30 totalling about 17 billion USD.

Subscription lines flatter early IRR because LP capital is called later. For vintages 2019 to 2022 funds with a line show an average IRR of 7.4 percent at eight quarters of age versus 2.3 percent for funds without (a gap of about 5 points). For mature vintages 2014 to 2017 the gap at 2026-06-30 is under 1.5 points. The Harborline watch threshold is a line balance above 15 percent of NAV.

Calder Ridge Capital Partners IV (FND-0117) is the hero fund: a 3.2 billion USD North American buyout fund of vintage 2018 managed by Calder Ridge Capital of Boston with a 400 million USD subscription line. At 2026-06-30 its NAV is 2614.0 million called capital 2880.0 million (90 percent paid in) distributions 1152.0 million line balance 210.0 million net IRR 18.4 percent TVPI 1.31 and DPI 0.40. In Q2 2026 it called 64.0 million (40.0 on 2026-04-14 and 24.0 on 2026-06-02) and distributed 96.0 million on 2026-05-20. Its matching benchmark HPCI-BUYOUT-NA vintage 2018 shows a pooled IRR of 14.6 percent.

The Calder Ridge IV Q2 2026 quarterly report to limited partners is attached as a document; FUND_REPORT_EXTRACTS holds the figures the extraction pipeline (harborline-docai-2.3) read from it and they match the published figures exactly with confidence 0.97.

FUND_REPORT_EXTRACTS covers the two latest quarters (2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30) for every active fund (711 extractions). About 91 percent are AUTO_ACCEPTED; extractions with confidence below 0.90 go to ANALYST_REVIEW and CORRECTED rows were fixed by an analyst. V_REPORT_EXTRACTION_RECONCILIATION compares each extraction with the published NAV calls distributions and line balance.

Distribution drought: vintages 2021 and 2022 have a median DPI of about 0.16 at sixteen quarters of age against 0.55 to 0.60 for vintages 2014 to 2016 at the same age. Distributions across the universe in the first half of 2026 (about 36 billion USD) are roughly 44 percent below the first half of 2021 (about 64 billion USD).

Cash-flow pacing questions use V_CASH_FLOW_PACING_QUARTERLY: calls distributions and net cash flow per fund and quarter with FUND_AGE_QUARTERS so vintages can be compared at the same age. Net cash flow is distributions minus calls and is negative during the investment period (the J-curve).

Allocators are Harborline's limited-partner clients on the portal: Westbrook State Retirement System (public pension) Thornfield University Endowment Marrow Lake Insurance Group Pelham Family Office and Northern Harbour Sovereign Fund. ALLOCATOR_COMMITMENTS lists their commitments to covered funds; V_ALLOCATOR_HOLDINGS and V_ALLOCATOR_VINTAGE_VS_BENCHMARK compare them to the matching benchmarks.

Westbrook State Retirement System (ALC-001) has 38 covered commitments totalling 2.71 billion USD. Its 2018 vintage sleeve (8 funds 760 million USD committed) lags its matching benchmarks by about 3.5 points (portfolio IRR 8.5 percent versus 12.0 percent) because of two North American venture funds: Bramblewood Ventures III (IRR about -3.5 percent 15.7 points below the HPCI-VENTURE-NA 2018 index) and Sable Point Ventures II (IRR about 0.1 percent 12.2 points below). Every other Westbrook vintage is at or above benchmark.

IRR TVPI DPI and RVPI are net to LPs. TVPI = (NAV + cumulative distributions) / cumulative called; DPI = cumulative distributions / cumulative called; RVPI = NAV / cumulative called. They are NULL until a fund has called at least 2 percent of commitments.

QUARTERLY_RETURN_PCT is the net time-weighted return for the quarter: (closing NAV minus opening NAV plus distributions minus calls) divided by opening NAV. Pooled index quarterly return is NAV-weighted. Never average IRR columns across quarters; IRR is a since-inception figure that already compounds.

FUND_STATUS is INVESTING for funds within five years of first call HARVESTING afterwards and LIQUIDATED once the fund has distributed its final value (25 funds mostly vintages 2012 and 2013). Liquidated funds stop reporting so their latest row is earlier than 2026-06-30.

Portal tiers: Standard clients receive the published indices; Premium Analytics clients can build custom indices pacing views and portfolio-versus-benchmark comparisons. The premium tier is the conversational analytics product this domain supports.
